# XDR205: decoder with limits disabled

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | XDR2xx: missing depth and size caps |
| How to fix | decode with limits: keep the default MaxDepth and set MaxInputLen, or use xdr.SafeUnmarshal |
| Default severity | error (`severity: {XDR205: …}` changes it) |
| Default rule set | yes |
| Guide | [Recommendations for meta readers](../../guide/indexer-hardening.mdx#caps-meta-readers) |
| Self-audit checklist item | HC-204 |
| Demonstrating corpus entry | `limits/scvec-nesting-100` (registered in [corpus/plan.json](../../corpus/plan.json)) |
| Fixtures | [lint/testdata/xdr2xx/xdr205](../testdata/xdr2xx/xdr205) |

## What it reports

- An error for any use of go-xdr's `DecodeUnlimitedDepth`, or a `DecodeOptions` literal whose `MaxDepth` is an
  unlimited sentinel.
- A warning for `xdr.Unmarshal` or `xdr.UnmarshalWithOptions` on a reader without a `Len() int` method (a network
  body, a decompression stream) when `MaxInputLen` is not set.

`xdr.SafeUnmarshal…` with its defaults is not reported: depth 1500, the input length set, pre-allocation capped.

## Why it matters

The decoder's limits are what bound everything a reader does afterwards. With the depth limit disabled, one
deeply nested value exhausts the stack; with no input length, a length prefix can claim more data than the
stream holds. The go-xdr default of 1500 depth units admits 749 nested vector levels, more than stellar-core
admits into a ledger, so the defaults are safe for ledger meta.

## Example

Reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr2xx/xdr205/bad.go
// Depth unlimited, from a network body.
func decodeUnlimited(body io.Reader) (xdr.ScVal, error) {
	var v xdr.ScVal
	_, err := xdr.UnmarshalWithOptions(body, &v, xdr.DecodeOptions{MaxDepth: xdr3.DecodeUnlimitedDepth})
	return v, err
}
```

Not reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr2xx/xdr205/good.go
// A stream with MaxInputLen set.
func decodeLimited(r io.Reader, n int) (xdr.ScVal, error) {
	var v xdr.ScVal
	_, err := xdr.UnmarshalWithOptions(r, &v, xdr.DecodeOptions{MaxInputLen: n})
	return v, err
}
```

## Limits

Options held in a variable instead of a literal are not examined.

## Configure and suppress

Turn the rule off by leaving XDR205 out of `rules` in `.xdrlint.yml` or a profile. To accept one report, put `//xdrlint:ignore XDR205 <reason>` on the reported line or on the enclosing function's doc comment (under golangci-lint, `//nolint:xdrlint // <reason>`), or add an entry to an external suppression file for code you cannot edit. A suppression needs a reason, and one that suppresses nothing is itself reported (XDR000). See [Configuring and suppressing](README.md#linter-suppressions).
